# Mahāpaññākathā (Ps 3.1)
**ID:** Ps 3.1
**Section:** Paṭisambhidāmagga (ps)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-2

**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ps3.1
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0517m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mahāpaññākathā* ("Discussion of Great Wisdom", Ps 3.1) is the opening discourse of the third division (*Mahāvagga* or third *paṇṇāsaka*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, spanning pages 190–202 in the second volume of the Pali Text Society edition [Bodhi 2003]. The text is an extensive analytical treatise defining various gradations and modes of wisdom (*paññā*). Among these, it specifies that one is endowed with "great wisdom" (*mahāpañña*) by virtue of possessing great morality, concentration, wisdom, and liberation, meditative dwellings and attainments, development of the thirty-seven requisites of enlightenment, noble paths, fruitions, direct knowledges, and the attainment of Nibbāna; it similarly defines "wide wisdom" (*puthupañña*) as wisdom directed toward the diverse aggregates, elements, and sense bases [Bodhi 2003].
SuttaCentral registers a direct passage-level parallel to the *Mahāpaññākathā* in the *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16) of the *Mahāniddesa*, noting related thematic mentions in the *Sotāpattiphalasutta* (SN 55.55), SN 55.56–74, the *Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 19), *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), *Pasūrasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 8), and the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus demonstrates substantial text reuse with these same texts, showing extended shared segments with Mnd 16 (especially §26.6–29.4), Cnd 19, Mnd 14, Mnd 8, and the *Sotāpatti Saṁyutta* (SN 55), alongside significant self-reuse with the *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1) and extensive borrowing in the commentaries to the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* and the *Theragāthā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages with Sanskrit and Tibetan works, notably the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, and the *Mahāvyutpatti* [DharmaNexus].
